Qiangtang Terrane and its implications for uplift and southward
crustal extrusion in the southeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau

Keywords:
Paleogene crustal shortening before 54–43 Ma, indicating the uplift of southern and central Tibet in the early
paleomagnetism Eocene. Subsequently, since 35.4 ± 2.4 Ma, the north of the Qiangtang Terrane experienced ∼1300 ±
Qiangtang Terrane 410 km of crustal shortening, indicating the uplift of the northern Tibetan Plateau. The Lhasa Terrane
southward extrusion and Qiangtang Terrane have not experienced further crustal shortening since the late Eocene, and
Tibetan Plateau uplift the southeastern part of Tibet cannot have provided abundant crustal material to accommodate the
significant crustal southward extrusion in the southeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau. The crust of
the Tengchong Terrane and Shan–Thai Block did not experience significant southward extrusion since the
late Oligocene–Early Miocene. The Indochina Block was situated in the north of the Qiangtang Terrane
before the Oligocene, and since the early Oligocene, the Indochina Block began to experience southward
extrusion from the north of the Qiangtang Terrane, which absorbed part of the crustal shortening in the
north of the Qiangtang Terrane.

Overall, the geological evidence indicates that the Gonjo and Ran-
mugou Formations were formed in the Eocene. 3. Methods
The sampling section was distributed in the two limbs of a fold.

N is the number of sampling sites used for paleomagnetic calculation. Dec. and Inc. are declination and inclination, respectively. Plat. and Plon. are latitude and longitude of paleopoles. α 95 and A95 is the radius of cone at 95
percent confidence level about the mean direction. dp/dm is the confidence limits of poles. Paleolat. is the calculated paleolatitude, positive means the north latitude, negative means the south latitude. # means the paleomagnetic
data were not used in the discussion. Time (Ma): P, Paleocene. E, Eocene. Rock type: R. Red-beds; V, volcanic rock; La, lava flow; T, tuff; D, dyke; A, Andesite; Li, limestone. Fold Test: P, positive fold test; M, the A95 value of
the mean VGP of sampling section falls just within the range of A95 values defined as a reliability envelope by Deenen et al.(2011); D, coexistence of dual-polarity. Inclination Shallowing correction: N, not applied inclination
shallowing correction; E, E/I correction; A, anisotropy-based inclination correction.

### page_9
Y.Tongetal./EarthandPlanetaryScienceLetters475(2017)1–14 9
shortening process indicates that southern and central Tibet prob-
ably experienced initial uplift in the Early Eocene, and that subse-
quently, the north of the QT began to uplift since the late Eocene
(35.4±2.4 Ma). The deep seismic reflection profile across the
Yarlung Zangbo Suture shows that the deepest part of the Indian
crust is underthrust just to the north of the YZS (Gao et al., 2016).
This indicates that the crustal thrusting and folding movement of
the interior of the Tibetan Plateau was probably the principal cause
of the uplifting of the Plateau.
Numerous geological studies also suggest that southern Tibet
had already been uplifted in the Eocene. The reconstructed paleo-
elevations in the Himalaya and the LT show that the southern
Tibetan Plateau had already been uplifted to near-modern altitudes
in the late Oligocene (Currie et al., 2005; Mulch and Chamberlain,
2006; Polissar et al., 2009; Xu et al., 2010; DeCelles et al., 2011);
and that the LT, in particular, had been uplifted to an elevation of
more than 4000 m before the Oligocene (Rowley and Currie, 2006;

Fig.6.(A) Equal-area projection of paleopoles of LT with the age of 54–43Ma. Small-circle fitting passes through 2 selected Paleogene poles of the LT and gives a paleolatitude
of 22.6◦ ±0.7◦N (reference point: 30.0◦N, 91.0◦E). The expected Paleogene poles of the reference point (30.0◦N, 91.0◦E) is 33.4 ◦ ±2.9◦N. (B) Equal-area projection of the
64–53Ma paleopoles of the LT. The LT was situated at the paleolatitude of 7.5◦ ±8.5◦N in 64–60 Ma,then moved to the paleolatitude of 13.7◦±7.3◦N at 55Ma, and finally
arrived the paleolatitude of 16.5◦ ±5.7◦N at 53Ma. The expected Paleogene poles of the reference point (30.0◦N, 91.0◦E) is 33.4◦ ±2.9◦N. (C)Equal-area projection of
the late Eocene paleopoles of the central part of the QT. Small-circle fitting passes through 2 selected poles gives a paleolatitude of 11.2◦±3.6◦N (reference point: 30.0◦N,
91.0◦E). The expected Paleogene poles of the reference point (30.0◦N, 91.0◦E) is 33.4◦ ±2.9◦N. (D)Equal-area projection of Eocene paleopoles of the eastern part of the QT.
The eastern part of the QT was situated at the paleolatitude of 23.9◦ ±2.9◦N in the period of 56.0–43.2Ma. The expected Paleogene poles of the reference point (31.0◦N,
98.2◦E) is 35.5◦ ±2.7◦N.
Fig.7.The Cenozoic crustal movement characteristic of the southeastern part of the Tibet. The Indochina Block was situated at the north of the QT. Since the Oligocene –
Early Miocene, the TCT and STB began southeastward clockwise rotational scattering movement in the form of ductile deformation. Since the early Oligocene, the ICB began
to experience southward extrusion from the north of the QT, which absorbed part of the crustal shortening in the north of the QT.
